transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um... well, my wife wanted me to come. Her and... my supervisor at work. 

They just keep getting mad, saying I'm not listening. Like, they'll be talking right to me, and... I don't know, a minute later I realize I only caught half of what they said. Then I have to ask them to say it again. So... yeah. That's why I'm here.
Have you struggled with this kind of inattentiveness since you were a child, or is this something that has only started more recently?

Yeah... it's always been like this. Even back when I was a kid. 

Um... teachers were always moving my seat. Said I couldn't stay put. I guess I... called out answers a lot, too. Got in some trouble for butting into other kids' work... back before middle school. So, yeah. Not a new thing.
Do you still find it difficult to sit still or do you often feel the need to be constantly on the go?

Yeah... I guess so. Um, from the time I clock in till I get home, I'm... I'm always jumping to the next thing. Work orders, pickup, dinner, laundry. Just always moving. And... I don't know, even when there's a quiet minute, I just... I can't really sit down and rest. It's just how I am.
When you are in situations where you are expected to stay seated, like during a long meeting or while watching a movie, do you find it very difficult to remain in your seat for the duration?

Yeah... I guess. I don't really do meetings much. But at work... they expect me to stay at my station. 

And I just... I end up stepping away a lot. You know, to check something, or grab a tool. Or just... talk to somebody. Even though I know the line needs me right there, I just... yeah. I don't stay put very well.
Do you feel that these challenges with staying focused or sitting still have caused significant problems in your personal life or your ability to keep up with your responsibilities outside of work?

Yeah... it causes problems. 

At work... they've given me formal warnings. It's gotten serious. I mean... I worry about losing the job. Or... you know, causing a safety issue on the line because I'm not where I'm supposed to be. 

And at home... my wife gets pretty fed up. The kids, too. I guess I just... I disrupt things. The routines and stuff. Instead of helping... I just kind of mess it up. So... yeah. It's a problem.
